title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 2nd District
area: Parts of Philadelphia and Montgomery County.

context.text: Brendan Boyle advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. Jessica Arriaga won the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Brendan Boyle is the Democratic incumbent, a Philadelphia native who served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2009 to 2015 before his election to Congress in 2014. He is the ranking member of the House Budget Committee and also serves on the Ways and Means Committee. According to his official biography, he is a visiting lecturer at Princeton University and lead Democrat on the U.S. delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia in 1977; his official biography says he was born and raised in the city, the son of an immigrant, with a father who worked as a SEPTA janitor and a mother who was a school crossing guard.

First in his family to attend college; earned a bachelor's degree in government from the University of Notre Dame (1999) and a Master of Public Policy from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government (2005).
Worked for American Management Systems as a consultant, as a radio broadcaster and as an adjunct professor before entering office.
Elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2008 and served from 2009 to 2015; according to his official biography, he was the first Democrat to represent his legislative district.
His brother, Kevin Boyle, was elected to the state House in 2010, which his official biography describes as making them the first brothers to serve together in that chamber.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2014; his official biography describes the win as an upset over three better-funded rivals, and says he is now in his sixth term.
In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), is ranking member of the House Budget Committee and serves on the Ways and Means Committee's Health and Trade subcommittees.

Serves as lead Democrat for the U.S. congressional delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, is a visiting lecturer at Princeton University, and co-chairs several caucuses including the Auto Care, Blue Collar and EU caucuses, according to his official pages.

record.text: Serves as ranking member (top Democrat) of the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress.
Serves on the Ways and Means Committee's Health and Trade subcommittees in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Jessica Arriaga
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Jessica Arriaga is the Republican nominee, a healthcare professional from North Philadelphia. Her campaign says she has worked in operating rooms for more than 20 years and describes herself as a mother. She advanced unopposed from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary and is running on a message of results-focused leadership for Philadelphia families.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she was born and raised in North Philadelphia and is a mother.
Has worked in operating rooms as a healthcare professional for more than 20 years, and says she has also helped families in her community find healthcare, resources and opportunity.
Describes herself as "not a career politician" and says she is not backed by political insiders.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for Pennsylvania's 2nd District with 100% of 6,328 votes, with no other candidate on the ballot.

priorities.text: Campaign messaging centers on rising costs, public safety and fewer opportunities for Philadelphia families, and presents herself as a political outsider not backed by "political insiders."
